canDo: Can combine cause (puisque, étant donné que, faute de), concession (bien que, certes… mais, avoir beau) and hypothesis (si + plus-que-parfait / past conditional, à condition que) in the same argument, stating a position clearly and responding to the other side, in writing and speech.
review: Integrated review of days 1–13: choice of mood (bien que / à condition que + subjunctive, même si / puisque + indicative), logical connectors, past tenses and time conjunctions, indirect speech and passive structures; focus on days 5, 7 and 9 (cause, concession and hypothesis).
input: Read: an investigative report on loneliness, an opinion piece against “compulsory civic service” and a forum post about a neighbourhood meal that fell flat (mark every cause, concession and hypothesis and check the mood); listen: a radio debate on intergenerational home-sharing, a segment on “third places” and a vox pop on relations between neighbours (note both sides’ arguments and concessions).
output: Write: a forum reply (≥220 words) taking a position on “should every citizen have to volunteer every month?” and responding to opposing arguments; speak: a 3-minute monologue on moving all administrative procedures online, then a debate on “closing neighbourhood council offices”.
checkpoint: Reading and listening accuracy ≥80%; at least 2 each of cause, concession and hypothesis structures in the essay, all in the correct mood; a 3-minute monologue without breaking off, answering every objection in the debate with “concession + rebuttal”.
challenge: Today’s challenge: find a social news item on RFI’s « Journal en français facile » or TV5MONDE (housing, loneliness, volunteering, public services…) and write 3 sentences of opinion: one explaining a cause with étant donné que, one conceding with bien que, and one imagining “if only…” with si + plus-que-parfait; then record a 1-minute spoken response.

questions.why: The article covers in turn the survey data, causes, consequences, responses and demands. B: the researchers in the text are cautious about social media; C: the café in Nantes is just one example.

« Plus surprenant encore, vivre entouré ne protège pas toujours : près d’une personne sur dix vivant en couple ou en famille déclare se sentir souvent seule. » A: the text makes no such comparison; C shifts the meaning: “one in five” refers to “not having had a real conversation in a month”, not to living alone.
« les chercheurs restent prudents… Tout dépend, en somme, de l’usage qu’on en fait. » A and B are absolute claims.
faute de + noun = for lack of…, expressing a cause. B expresses concession, the opposite meaning; C misreads faute as “fault”.
avoir beau + infinitive = however much… (concession). A mistakes concession for cause and effect; C contradicts “on a small scale”.

The unreal past hypothesis « Si l’on avait pris le problème au sérieux il y a dix ans, nous n’en serions pas là » implies a reproach that the issue wasn’t taken seriously. A: she only warns against stopping at awareness campaigns; B isn’t mentioned.
« on ne fabrique pas de la solidarité par décret. On la rend possible, on l’encourage ». A is the view he opposes; C contradicts his point about lack of funding and places.
« J’en sais quelque chose… nos meilleurs bénévoles sont précisément ceux qui ont choisi de venir. » B and C have no basis, and C is the opposite of “our best volunteers”.
« beaucoup de jeunes ne s’engagent pas faute d’en avoir eu l’occasion… C’est un argument sérieux. » A: he thinks the cost would be huge; B doesn’t appear in the text.

si + plus-que-parfait / past conditional expresses something contrary to past fact: the implication is that the project was never properly costed. A is the opposite of the implication; C (“lying deliberately”) reads too much into it.
par décret = by administrative order; the sentence means solidarity can’t be created by decree. B is the opposite of the author’s view; C twists it into a question of efficiency.
« Quelles idées ont fonctionné chez vous ? Je suis preneuse de tous vos conseils ». A isn’t an invitation post; B: she doesn’t complain about her neighbours’ behaviour.
It fell from « une soixantaine » to « une quinzaine ». B and C don’t match the figures.
« parce que les nouveaux habitants ne se sentent pas invités, puisqu’ils ne connaissent personne ? » A isn’t mentioned; C: she says posters went up in every stairwell.
« C’est possible. Mais je n’ai pas envie de transformer un moment convivial en kermesse. » A: she has reservations; C: she doesn’t reject the suggestion on grounds of cost.
« une formule qui séduit de plus en plus : la cohabitation entre étudiants et personnes âgées ». B is only mentioned at the end; C isn’t covered.
« Étant donné que les loyers ne cessent d’augmenter dans les villes universitaires, la demande des étudiants explose. » Neither A nor C is mentioned.

« Disons que je suis enthousiaste, mais lucide. Bien que ces expériences soient souvent très réussies, elles ne concernent qu’un nombre limité de personnes. » Neither A nor B matches his concessive position.
She thought the student would have dinner with her every evening, « alors que lui imaginait une simple colocation » — they had different expectations. A isn’t mentioned; C is the opposite.
« nous organisons plusieurs rencontres, et une charte est signée par les deux parties ». B isn’t mentioned; C: the charter only “sets” rules for visits, it doesn’t ban them.
« elle ne doit pas servir d’excuse aux pouvoirs publics », and he uses si + plus-que-parfait to say that student housing should have been funded earlier. A and B aren’t mentioned.
It opens with the topic « les tiers-lieux », and the whole segment covers their definition, why they succeed, their difficulties and their social role. B and C are only examples.
« beaucoup de lieux de rencontre ont disparu… Les tiers-lieux comblent ce vide. » Neither A nor C is mentioned.
« de bénévoles qui finissent par s’épuiser, et de subventions qui peuvent s’arrêter du jour au lendemain ». A isn’t mentioned; B contradicts “very successful”.
« Ils ne se seraient jamais parlé ailleurs. C’est peut-être ça, le vrai service rendu par ces lieux. » A and C misread details.
« il faut dire que j’habite le même immeuble depuis trente ans ». Neither B nor C is mentioned.
« bien que je dise bonjour à tout le monde… personne ne m’a encore invité ». A isn’t mentioned; C: he only imagines moving to a village, he doesn’t say he comes from one.
« je connais surtout ceux qui ont des enfants, puisque nos enfants vont à la même école ». Neither A nor B is mentioned.

V14-02.zh: because of, as a result of … (written)
V14-02.exZh: Because of job mobility, many people live far from their families.

V14-03.exZh: Thanks to video calls, she keeps in touch with her grandchildren.

V14-07.exZh: If we had acted sooner, we wouldn’t be where we are now.

V14-08.exZh: For six months, he carried out a public-interest assignment in a school.

V14-09.exZh: After the flood, the villagers pulled together again.

V14-10.exZh: The plan has a laudable intention, but it remains unrealistic.

V14-11.exZh: The intention is good, but the method seems wrong to me.

V14-12.zh: to know a thing or two about it
V14-12.exZh: Volunteering can change a life — I know a thing or two about it.

V14-13.exZh: You can’t make people show solidarity by decree.

V14-14.exZh: However much I rack my brains, I can’t find a solution.

V14-15.exZh: I welcome all your ideas, even the simplest ones.

V14-16.exZh: Before moving in, the student and the host must sign a charter.

V14-17.zh: to get something out of it (both sides)
V14-17.exZh: When the rules are clear, both sides get something out of it.

V14-18.exZh: Does the state really need to get involved in this?

V14-19.exZh: This initiative must not serve as an excuse for the public authorities.

V14-20.exZh: Seeing a lonely neighbour smile again is priceless.

V14-21.exZh: Since the café closed, this community venue has filled a gap in the village.

V14-22.exZh: The project is appealing, but it isn’t all rosy.

V14-23.exZh: Without lasting funding, these venues may close.

V14-24.exZh: Many employees care for a parent and are short of time.

V14-25.exZh: Associations are asking for every town hall to keep an in-person reception desk.
